title: Euler's identity applied to the dilates g(t⁻¹·): n·∫ g(t⁻¹y) dμ + ∫ Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) dμ = 0
statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N that is finite on compact sets and let n ∈ ℕ. Suppose that ∫ (n·h(y) + Dh(y)(y)) dμ(y) = 0 for every C¹ function h : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support (Dh = fderiv ℝ h). Then for every C¹ function g : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support and every t > 0, n·∫ g(t⁻¹y) dμ(y) + ∫ Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) dμ(y) = 0, where Dg = fderiv ℝ g.
lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → (∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∫ y, ((n : ℝ) * g y + fderiv ℝ g y y) ∂μ = 0) → ∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → (n : ℝ) * (∫ y, g (t⁻¹ • y) ∂μ) + ∫ y, fderiv ℝ g (t⁻¹ • y) (t⁻¹ • y) ∂μ = 0
